I am 70 years old and have been working this land for two decades. I know this county's soil and climate well. My 10.1 mu grows wheat in the winter and maize in the summer on the same plots — that is how we have always done it here in Quzhou. My body is slower now, so I hire a neighbor's son for heavy work at sowing and harvest. I keep things simple because I understand simple things.

**Wheat (October sow, June harvest):**
I will use the improved variety my village cooperative sells — better than the old seeds I saved years ago, neighbors get more per mu with it. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea at jointing, same as always. My well pump covers 3 irrigations: before winter freeze sets in, again at jointing, and once at heading. If summer stays dry last year taught me I need that heading water. I spray herbicide in late winter when the weeds come up, then fungicide twice around heading to prevent rust and powdery mildew — this region always gets it. I rotary till after maize harvest to chop the stover down before sowing wheat.

**Maize (June sow, October harvest):**
All hybrid seed now — even I know the old varieties cannot match hybrid yields. I broadcast base fertilizer before sowing and top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. I irrigate at emergence if it is dry, and again at silking — that silking water makes a real difference to the cob. I spray herbicide right after emergence and treat for corn borer once if I see the damage starting. After wheat harvest I do a light rotary pass to level the ground before planting.
